# Majid DS (mahdimajidzadeh/ds)

> RTL/Persian-first UI kit for Laravel Livewire, layered on top of Flux UI (livewire/flux, free tier).
> Adds an `mds:` Blade component namespace next to `flux:`: Persian digits/money, Jalali dates,
> Hugeicons in place of heroicons, e-commerce components, and open implementations of Flux Pro's command
> palette, composer, color picker, file upload, timeline and chart.
> This file is the complete machine-oriented API reference. Human docs: docs/index.html.

Requirements: PHP 8.2+, Laravel 11+, Livewire 3, Tailwind CSS v4. `livewire/flux ^2.0` is installed automatically.

## Setup contract

1. `composer require mahdimajidzadeh/ds` (service provider auto-discovered).
2. resources/css/app.css MUST import, in order:
   `@import 'tailwindcss';`
   `@import '../../vendor/livewire/flux/dist/flux.css';`
   `@import '../../vendor/mahdimajidzadeh/ds/resources/css/mds.css';`
   `@source '../../vendor/mahdimajidzadeh/ds/resources/views';`  <- REQUIRED: Tailwind v4 skips gitignored
   paths, so without this the utility classes inside the kit's Blade views are never generated.
   `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));`
3. Layout: `<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">`; `@fluxAppearance` in <head>; `@fluxScripts` before </body>. Load a Persian font yourself — see Fonts. Under a CSP, register the nonce with `Vite::useCspNonce()` — see Content Security Policy.
4. Alpine is REQUIRED for interactive components (input, quantity, countdown, rating.input, command, composer, color-picker, file-upload, preview-card, chart.heatmap).
   Livewire injects Alpine only on pages rendering a Livewire component; on static pages add `@livewireScripts`.
5. Tag syntaxes are equivalent: `<mds:rating />` === `<x-mds::rating />`. Subcomponents use dots: `<mds:command.item>`.
6. Components follow Flux's `--color-accent` theme tokens and support dark mode via the `.dark` class.

## Config (config/mds.php; publish tag `mds-config`)

- `mds.currency` (default `'toman'`): default currency for price component/directives/helpers. Values: `toman` | `rial` | `none` | any literal label string.
- `mds.persian_digits` (default `true`): global default for Persian output — digits, separators, AND every built-in string (unit labels, empty states, aria-labels). `false` = Latin digits + English strings throughout. Every component overrides per-instance via `:fa="true|false"`.
- `mds.icons.default` (default `'hugeicons'`): icon set for `<mds:icon>` and every mds component's `icon` prop. `'flux'` reverts the whole kit to heroicons.
- `mds.icons.style` (default `'stroke-rounded'`): Hugeicons style used when a component doesn't ask for one.
- `mds.icons.fallback_style` (default `true`): fall back to the free Stroke Rounded set when a requested Pro style isn't registered.
- `mds.icons.strict` (default `false`): `true` makes `<mds:icon>` render nothing (instead of `flux:icon`/heroicons) for a name no Hugeicons source has — use it to guarantee heroicons never render on pages that only call `<mds:icon>`.
- `mds.icons.sets` (default `[]`): `style => directory of .svg` for Hugeicons Pro exports. Each becomes a blade-icons set named `mds-hugeicons-{style}`. No Pro file is ever shipped with this package.

Publish tags: `mds-config` (config), `mds-views` (Blade views -> resources/views/mds/, app copies override package), `mds-assets` (mds.css copy).

## Fonts

The kit ships and loads NO font, and sets no `--font-sans` — the app owns typography. For Persian text set a Persian face as
Tailwind's sans family in resources/css/app.css, after the kit's import:
    `@theme { --font-sans: 'Vazirmatn', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; }`
Vazirmatn (SIL OFL) is the recommended default: one family, Persian and Latin on one scale. Two ways to load it:
- Self-hosted (recommended for traffic from Iran, where Google Fonts is slow or blocked; also avoids third-party requests):
  put the woff2 files under public/fonts and declare `@font-face { font-family: 'Vazirmatn'; src: url('/fonts/Vazirmatn[wght].woff2') format('woff2'); font-weight: 100 900; font-display: swap; }`.
- Google Fonts: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Vazirmatn:wght@100..900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">` in <head>.
Every mds component renders in the page's `font-sans`, so this one token styles the whole kit. (The `@mdsFonts` directive that used
to emit the Google Fonts tags was removed — replace it with one of the two above.)

## Content Security Policy

The interactive components register Alpine in inline `<script>` blocks, so a `script-src 'nonce-…'` policy needs the nonce.
Register it once per request with Laravel — `$nonce = Vite::useCspNonce();` in the CSP middleware — and the kit's scripts
carry it: every `<script>` in the kit renders `@mdsNonce`, which echoes `Mds::cspNonce()` (= `Vite::cspNonce()`) or nothing.
Livewire's `@livewireScripts` read the same registry; Flux takes it as an option: `@fluxAppearance(['nonce' => Vite::cspNonce()])`
and `@fluxScripts(['nonce' => Vite::cspNonce()])`. There is no kit-specific setter or config key on purpose.
A strict policy also needs `'unsafe-eval'` in script-src (Alpine's standard build, bundled by Livewire, evaluates `x-data`
expressions) and `'unsafe-inline'` in style-src (the kit renders inline `style` attributes: chart geometry, colour swatches,
hidden-until-Alpine states). Nonces cover scripts only.

## Blade directives

- `@fa($value)` -> Persian digits only ("order 123" -> "order ۱۲۳")
- `@faNum($value)` -> number with Persian separators (2500000 -> ۲٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰)
- `@toman($amount)` -> ۲٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان
- `@rial($amount)` -> ۹۹۰ ریال
- `@jalali($date)` -> ۲۹ مرداد ۱۴۰۵ (fixed 'j F Y'; custom formats via Mds::jalali())
- `@mdsNonce` -> `nonce="…"` for an inline `<script>` when the app registered a CSP nonce with `Vite::useCspNonce()`, else nothing. Every `<script>` in the kit carries it — see Content Security Policy

`@fa`/`@faNum`/`@toman`/`@rial` are Persian by definition (they ignore `mds.persian_digits`);
`@jalali` follows the config like the components — "29 Mordad 1405" when it is off.

## PHP API

Facade `MajidDs\Mds`:
- `Mds::fa($v): string` — digit conversion
- `Mds::number($v, int $decimals = 0): string`
- `Mds::money($amount, ?string $currency = null, int $decimals = 0): string` — always Persian (backs `@toman`); use `<mds:price>` for config-aware money
- `Mds::toman($amount): string` / `Mds::rial($amount): string`
- `Mds::jalali($date, string $format = 'j F Y', ?bool $persianDigits = null): string`
- `Mds::ago($date, ?bool $persian = null): string` — «۳ ساعت پیش» / «۲ روز دیگر»; `false` -> "3 hours ago" / "in 2 days"
- `Mds::fileSize($bytes, ?bool $persianDigits = null): string` — «۱۵۹ کیلوبایت» / «۱٫۵ مگابایت»; `false` -> "159 KB" / "1.5 MB"
- `Mds::cspNonce(): ?string` — the nonce registered with `Vite::useCspNonce()`, or null (what `@mdsNonce` echoes)

`MajidDs\Support\Persian` (static): `digits`, `latinDigits` (Persian->Latin, for input normalization), `number`, `format($value, int $decimals = 0, ?bool $persian = null)` (a number in the caller's language — Persian digits+separators or Latin), `decimal($value, ?bool $persian = null)` (whole numbers stay whole, fractions keep one place — chart axes and tallies), `auto($value, ?bool $persian = null)` (int|float -> `format()`; a string keeps its shape and only its digits convert: '100%' -> '۱۰۰%'), `money` (always Persian), `currencyLabel($currency, ?bool $persian = null)` (تومان/ریال or Toman/Rial), `ago($date, ?bool $persian = null)`, `fileSize($bytes, ?bool $persianDigits = null)` (1024-based, 1 decimal below 100 and none for whole numbers; Persian units بایت/کیلوبایت/… or English B/KB/MB/GB/TB), `toDateTime` (DateTime|string|int -> DateTimeImmutable).

`MajidDs\Support\Jalali` (static, dependency-free, intl-verified):
- `fromGregorian(int $gy, int $gm, int $gd): array{0:int,1:int,2:int}` — e.g. (2026,8,20) -> [1405,5,29]
- `toGregorian(int $jy, int $jm, int $jd): array` — exact inverse
- `isLeapYear(int $year): bool` — whether Esfand has 30 days; agrees with the converters by construction
- `format($date, string $format = 'j F Y', ?bool $persianDigits = null): string` — `$persianDigits=false` gives Latin digits, transliterated month names (Farvardin…Esfand), English weekdays, AM/PM
- Format tokens: Y y n m j d F(month name) l/D(weekday name) + time passthroughs H G h g i s v, A/a (قبل‌ازظهر/بعدازظهر or AM/PM). Backslash escapes a token.
- Constants: `Jalali::MONTHS` (1-indexed Persian month names), `Jalali::WEEKDAYS` (keyed by PHP `w`, 0=Sunday).

`MajidDs\Support\Iran` (static, dependency-free; every method accepts Persian/Arabic-Indic digits and ignores spaces and dashes):
- `digits($value): string` — Latin digits and nothing else
- `nationalId($value): bool` — 10 digits, mod-11 check digit, repeated-digit IDs (1111111111) rejected
- `mobile($value): bool` · `normalizeMobile($value): ?string` — 0912…, 912…, +98912…, 0098912… all accepted; normalized to the 11-digit "09…" form, null when not a mobile number
- `sheba($value): bool` · `normalizeSheba($value): ?string` — IBAN mod-97 check; "IR" may be omitted on input; normalized to "IR" + 24 digits, no spaces
- `bankCard($value): bool` · `normalizeBankCard($value): ?string` — 16 digits passing Luhn; normalized to the digits alone

`MajidDs\Rules` — Laravel `ValidationRule` objects over those checks: `new NationalId`, `new IranMobile`, `new Sheba`, `new BankCard`. Each takes an
optional `?string $message`; otherwise the message is Persian or English by `config('mds.persian_digits')` and carries `:attribute`
(":attribute یک کد ملی معتبر نیست." / "The :attribute is not a valid national ID."). They accept exactly what the `mds:input.*` presets
produce — Persian digits, the mask's spaces, Sheba's IR prefix — so validate the raw value and store the `Iran::normalize*()` form.

`MajidDs\Support\Charts` (static, dependency-free SVG geometry behind the `mds:chart.*` stages; public because published views call it):
- `n(float $value): string` — coordinate rounded to 4 places (keeps rebuilds byte-identical)
- `points(array $values, float $x0, float $y0, float $width, float $height, float $max, float $min = 0): array` — series -> [[x, y], …] on a plot box
- `linePath(array $points): string` / `splinePath(array $points): string` — polyline, or a monotone cubic spline that never overshoots
- `closePath(string $path, float $left, float $right, float $baseline): string` — closes a trace down to the baseline for an area fill
- `polarPoint(float $cx, float $cy, float $r, float $bearing): array` · `arcPath(float $cx, float $cy, float $r, float $from, float $to): string` (bearings in degrees, 0 = 12 o'clock)
- `capDegrees(float $strokeWidth, float $r): float` — how far a round stroke cap overhangs an arc end, in degrees
- `barPath(float $x, float $y, float $w, float $h, array $radii): string` — rect with per-corner radii, clamped to the box
- `niceMax(float $max): float` · `ticks(float $max): array` — a "nice" axis ceiling and five ticks 0..ceiling

## Livewire/form binding contract

Components with values render a hidden `<input>`; `wire:model` attributes are forwarded to it and it dispatches
bubbling `input` events on every change. Hidden values are ALWAYS Latin digits / machine formats regardless of
Persian display. Applies to: quantity, rating.input, color-picker. `name="..."` enables plain form posts.
`<mds:input>` is the same rule for a visible text field: it is `flux:input` with the `x-mds-digits` directive, which rewrites
Persian/Arabic-Indic digits to Latin as they are typed or pasted, so the bound value is the machine form there too.

## Validation contract

Five controls take `error` string|null and `invalid` bool=false. An explicit `error` wins; when omitted and `name` is set, it
falls back to `$errors->first($name)` (file-upload also tries `$errors->first("$name.*")`, the shape `photos.*` rules produce).
Any error makes the control `invalid`. What that renders differs by design:
- **composer, color-picker, file-upload** sit in their own `flux:field`, so they render the message (flux:error markup, `role="alert"`).
- **quantity, rating.input** are primitives placed inside the app's own field, which already renders `flux:error` — so `error` only
  drives their state (`aria-invalid="true"`, red border on the stepper) and NO message block. Render the message in the surrounding field.

## `fa` inheritance

`fa` on a wrapper reaches the mds subcomponents it renders or wraps (via `@aware`), so `<mds:file-upload :fa="false">` renders an English
dropzone and `<mds:product-card :fa="false">` an English price/rating/badge. Carriers: chart -> every `chart.*` stage; color-picker ->
area/slider/dropper; command -> input/items; file-upload -> dropzone; file-item -> remove; product-card -> price/rating/discount-badge;
price -> discount-badge. An explicit `:fa` on the child still wins. Subcomponents therefore all accept `fa` themselves.

## Components

### <mds:input> — Flux's input, Latin digits whatever keyboard typed them
Props: `only` bool=false (keep digits alone; also sets `inputmode="numeric"` unless the caller passes their own — do NOT combine with
Flux's `mask`, which owns the value's shape; digits still arrive Latin under a mask) · `ltr` bool=false (adds
`data-ltr`, which mds.css keeps left-to-right and end-aligned inside an RTL form — `type="tel"` already gets that).
Everything else is `flux:input`'s own and passes through unchanged: `label`, `description`, `placeholder`, `icon`, `icon:trailing`,
`clearable`, `copyable`, `viewable`, `mask`, `type`, `size`, `invalid`, `wire:model`, `name`, `class` — including Flux's validation
state from `$errors` (so, like any flux:input, it needs the shared `$errors` bag: a real request, or `View::share('errors', new ViewErrorBag)`).
Renders `<input … x-mds-digits="" data-mds-input>` (`x-mds-digits.only=""` with `only`). The directive rewrites ۰-۹ and ٠-٩ to 0-9 in
`beforeinput` (typing, paste, drop), so the field fires ONE `input` event, already Latin, and undo history survives; IME composition text,
which cannot be intercepted there, is normalised on `input` with the caret restored and the event re-dispatched. The field therefore SHOWS
Latin digits — what is on screen is what posts. No `fa` prop: nothing here is display-only.
`x-mds-digits` is registered by the kit's shared script (`mds::partials.digits`), which is on the page whenever an mds:input, quantity,
countdown, composer, file-upload or command rendered; on such a page it may be put on any other input or textarea by hand.
Registration guards against Alpine having already started (a `wire:navigate` visit), so it works on navigated-to pages as well.
Iranian presets — each is `<mds:input>` with default attributes a caller's own attribute of the same name replaces; no props of their own:
- `<mds:input.mobile>` — `only ltr type="tel" maxlength="14" autocomplete="tel-national" placeholder="09123456789"`, marker `data-mds-input-mobile`. Value: the digits — 09… when typed, or a pasted 98…/0098… form (the cap is 14 so it is not truncated into a wrong number). Pair with the `IranMobile` rule and store `Iran::normalizeMobile()`.
- `<mds:input.national-id>` — `only ltr maxlength="10" autocomplete="off"`, marker `data-mds-input-national-id`. Value: the 10 digits. Pair with `NationalId`.
- `<mds:input.card>` — `ltr mask="9999 9999 9999 9999" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="cc-number" icon="credit-card"`, marker `data-mds-input-card`. NOT `only` (the mask owns the shape), so the bound value carries the spaces: "6037 9911 0000 0003". Pair with `BankCard`; store `Iran::normalizeBankCard()`.
- `<mds:input.sheba>` — `ltr mask="IR99 9999 9999 9999 9999 9999 99" inputmode="numeric"`, marker `data-mds-input-sheba`. The mask supplies the IR prefix and spacing; the user types 24 digits; the bound value is the spaced form. Pair with `Sheba`; store `Iran::normalizeSheba()`.

### <mds:rating> — star display
Props: `value` float=0 (clamped 0..max, fractions = partial fill) · `max` int=5 · `count` int|null=null (review count) · `size` sm|lg|default · `show-value` bool=true · `fa` bool|null=config.
Renders role="img" with `aria-label="{value} / {max}"` (digits follow `fa`). RTL-correct partial fill. Inherits `fa` from product-card.

### <mds:rating.input> — interactive stars
Props: `value` int=0 · `max` int=5 · `name` string|null · `size` sm|lg|default · `label` string|null='امتیاز' / 'Rating' by fa ·
`reverse` bool=false (flips Arrow Left/Right) · `error` / `invalid` (see Validation contract — state only, no message) · `fa` bool|null=config.
role="radiogroup" (aria-label = `label`, `aria-invalid` when invalid); each star is `role="radio"` + `aria-checked` + a digit aria-label.
Keyboard: ONE tab stop (the checked star, or the first when unset — roving tabindex). Arrow Right / Arrow Down = next star,
Arrow Left / Arrow Up = previous, Home/End = 1/max — the ARIA radio-group pattern, and the SAME mapping in RTL and LTR: nothing is
inferred from the page direction. In an RTL page the stars are laid out right-to-left, so Right moves the highlight visually leftward;
set `reverse` when you want Right to follow the visual row instead. Arrows both move focus and commit the value.
Hover preview; integer values; wire:model forwarded to the hidden input.

### <mds:price>
Props: `amount` number=0 · `original` number|null=null (compare-at; when > amount renders strikethrough + auto badge) · `currency` toman|rial|none|literal|null=config · `decimals` int=0 · `size` sm|lg|default · `fa` bool|null=config · `badge` bool=true (auto discount badge on/off).
Discount percent = round((1 - amount/original) * 100).

### <mds:discount-badge>
Props: `percent` int|null · `amount`+`original` number|null (computes percent when `percent` omitted and original > 0) · `size` sm|lg|default · `fa` (inherited from price/product-card).
Red pill, Persian percent sign ٪, `aria-label` «۲۵ درصد تخفیف» / "25% off". Renders NOTHING when no percent can be determined.

### <mds:quantity> — cart stepper
Props: `value` int|null=min · `min` int=1 · `max` int|null=null · `step` int=1 · `size` sm|lg|default · `name` · `fa` ·
`increment-label` / `decrement-label` (default 'افزایش تعداد'/'کاهش تعداد', or 'Increase quantity'/'Decrease quantity' when fa is off) ·
`error` / `invalid` (see Validation contract — red border + `aria-invalid`, no message).
`+` sits at inline-start (right in RTL). Buttons disable at bounds. `value` is clamped to [min, max] on the server too, so the first
paint and a no-JS post never sit outside the bounds. The displayed value is `aria-live="polite"`. Hidden input = Latin digits.

### <mds:product-card>
Props: `title` string='' · `image` string|null · `href` string|null · `amount`/`original` number|null · `currency` · `rating` float|null · `reviews` int|null · `badge` string|null (corner flux:badge text) · `badge-color` string='lime' (any Flux badge color) · `unavailable` bool=false (grayscale + «ناموجود», or "Out of stock" when fa is off) · `fa`.
Slot = actions area (e.g. add-to-cart flux:button). Composes flux:card + mds:rating + mds:price + mds:discount-badge.
With no `amount` and not `unavailable`, the price row is omitted entirely — a card is never shown at «۰ تومان» by accident.

### <mds:stepper> — checkout steps
Props: `steps` array=[] (labels in order) · `current` int=1 (1-based active index) · `fa`.
States: completed (check, accent) / current (aria-current="step") / upcoming (muted). data-mds-stepper-step attr per state.
Each step carries an sr-only «مرحله ۲ از ۴» / "Step 2 of 4" so a reader hears the position, not just the label.

### <mds:countdown>
Props: `until` DateTime|string REQUIRED · `days` bool=true (false = hours accumulate) · `labels` bool=false ·
`size` sm|lg|default · `fa` · `expired-text` string|null='به پایان رسید' / 'Expired' by fa.
Server-renders initial segments (no blank flash), ticks via a shared `Alpine.data('mdsCountdown')`; the interval stops at zero and
on component teardown (Livewire morph / wire:navigate), so nothing keeps ticking off-screen.
Accessibility: root is `role="timer"` with `aria-label` «زمان باقی‌مانده» / "Time remaining"; in the plain (unlabeled) variant each
box gets an sr-only unit (روز/ساعت/دقیقه/ثانیه or days/hours/min/sec) so it does not read as a bare run of digits.
Direction contract: plain variant is dir="ltr" wall-clock (۰۷:۴۱:۵۵ hours-first); `labels` variant is RTL boxes
(days rightmost) with روز/ساعت/دقیقه/ثانیه labels — Iranian e-commerce convention — or days/hours/min/sec when fa is off. Do not override.

### <mds:jalali-date>
Props: `date` DateTime|string|int REQUIRED · `format` string='j F Y' (Jalali tokens above) · `fa` · `ago` bool=false.
Renders `<time datetime="<gregorian ISO>">`; `ago` mode shows relative text with full Jalali date in title attr.
The calendar is always Jalali; `fa=false` switches the language: Latin digits, transliterated month names ("29 Mordad 1405"),
English weekday names, and English `ago` phrases ("2 days ago").

### <mds:empty-state>
Props: `icon` string|null (rendered through `<mds:icon>`, so a Hugeicons name wins and a heroicon name still resolves) · `title` string|null · `description` string|null. Slot = action buttons.

### <mds:preview-card> — hover preview of a link's destination
Compound: `<mds:preview-card>` (root) + `<mds:preview-card.trigger>` + `<mds:preview-card.content>`.
Root props: `delay` int=600 (hover-open ms) · `close-delay` int=300 (hover-close ms). Renders an inline wrapper holding state.
Trigger: a REAL `<a>` — pass `href` (+ any anchor attr); it navigates on click. Default styling `text-accent hover:underline`,
override with classes. Opens after `delay` on hover, immediately on keyboard focus; Escape closes.
Content props: `side` top|bottom|start|end='bottom' (logical: start/end follow the component's direction, so placement
mirrors on RTL pages — including RTL islands inside LTR pages) · `align` start|center|end='center' · `side-offset`
int=10 (6 when `arrow` is false) · `arrow` bool=true. Width via class (default `w-72`); `!p-0 overflow-hidden` for
image-led cards.
Behavior (Alpine): the popup is wrapped in `<template x-teleport="body">` — the template keeps a block-level card legal
inside a `<p>` (the parser would otherwise close the paragraph and reparent the popup out of scope) and teleports it to
body. Positioned `fixed` from measured rects; flips to the opposite side when out of room, clamps to the viewport
(5px padding), repositions on scroll/resize, and the arrow tracks the middle of the link. Transitions are skipped
under prefers-reduced-motion.
Accessibility: the preview is supplementary — it never opens on touch and is not announced to screen readers.
Do not put unique or essential content in it; keep that on the linked page.
```blade
<p>
    این کیت توسط
    <mds:preview-card>
        <mds:preview-card.trigger href="/team">@majid_ds</mds:preview-card.trigger>
        <mds:preview-card.content side="top" align="start">
            <div class="font-semibold">مجید دیزاین سیستم</div>
            <p>کیت رابط کاربری راست‌چین برای Laravel Livewire.</p>
        </mds:preview-card.content>
    </mds:preview-card>
    نگه‌داری می‌شود.
</p>
```

### <mds:command> — command palette (open version of Flux Pro's flux:command)
Wrapper holds state (shared `Alpine.data('mdsCommand')`). Props: `fa` bool|null=config (inherited by input/items). Compose:
- `<mds:command.input>` props: `icon`='magnifying-glass' · `clearable` bool=false · `closable` bool=false (closes containing <dialog>/Flux modal) · `clear-label` / `close-label` (default 'پاک کردن'/'بستن', or 'Clear'/'Close' by fa) · `fa` · plus any input attrs (placeholder, autofocus). Pass a `placeholder` or `aria-label`: the combobox has no built-in name.
- `<mds:command.items>` props: `empty` (no-results text; default 'نتیجه‌ای یافت نشد.', or 'No results found.' by fa) · `fa`. Scrollable wrapper around the listbox.
- `<mds:command.item>` props: `icon` · `icon-variant`='micro' · `kbd` string|null (rendered LTR at inline-end) · `href` (renders <a>; else <button type="button">). wire:click / x-on:click pass through.
- `<mds:command.heading>` — group label, auto-hides while a query is typed.
Behavior: live filter with Persian normalization (Arabic ي/ك -> ی/ک; Persian/Arabic-Indic digits -> Latin before matching);
ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active item; Enter clicks it; hover syncs active state; built-in empty state.
ARIA contract: the input is `role="combobox"` `aria-expanded="true"` `aria-autocomplete="list"` with `aria-controls` -> the listbox
and `aria-activedescendant` -> the active option (option ids are assigned at init). Items sit in `role="listbox"`, each `role="option"`
+ `aria-selected`; the heading is `role="presentation"`; the empty message is a `role="status"` region OUTSIDE the listbox.
The option list is cached for speed but follows the DOM: a MutationObserver on the palette re-scans when a Livewire morph or an
Alpine `x-for` adds, removes or relabels items, keeping the cursor on the same item where it survives. Server-filtered palettes
therefore work; `refresh()` on the Alpine component is public should a consumer ever need to force a re-scan.
Global ⌘K pattern (Flux free modal): `<flux:modal.trigger name="search" shortcut="cmd.k"><flux:input as="button" .../></flux:modal.trigger>`
+ `<flux:modal name="search" variant="bare" class="my-[12vh] w-full max-w-[30rem]"><mds:command>...</mds:command></flux:modal>`.

### <mds:composer> — chat/prompt input (open version of Flux Pro's flux:composer)
A textarea plus an action bar in one grid: `[leading actions][input][input][trailing actions]`.
Props: `name` string|null (plain form post + the key `$errors` is read with) · `value` string|null (initial text; the default
slot works too) · `placeholder` · `label`/`description` (flux:field chrome) · `label:sr-only` / `description:sr-only`
(Flux's colon syntax; `label-sr-only` / `description-sr-only` are equivalent) · `rows` int=2 (starting height in lines) ·
`max-rows` int|null (growth ceiling; unbounded when absent, never below `rows`) · `maxlength` int|null · `counter` bool=false ·
`inline` bool=false (actions beside the input instead of under it) · `variant` input|null (input = form-control corner radius) ·
`submit` cmd+enter|enter='cmd+enter' · `autofocus` bool=false · `dir` string|null (`auto` follows what is being typed) ·
`disabled` bool=false · `invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is set, falls back
to `$errors->first($name)`) · `fa` bool|null=config.
Slots: `input` (replaces the built-in textarea — this is where Flux puts its Pro editor) · `header` (above the input:
attachment previews, a reply-to line) · `footer` (under the action bar, sharing its row with the counter) ·
`actionsLeading` · `actionsTrailing` (usually the submit button).
`wire:model` is forwarded to the textarea; everything else lands on the root `[data-mds-composer]` div.
Behavior (Alpine): the textarea grows from `rows` to `max-rows` and then scrolls; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter calls
`form.requestSubmit()` on the enclosing form in both modes; `submit="enter"` additionally sends on a bare Enter, leaving
Shift+Enter as the newline; an open IME composition keeps its Enter. Auto-growing, the counter and bare-Enter submit all
belong to the built-in textarea, so an `input` slot brings its own (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter still works). Livewire clearing the
bound property from the server re-syncs the height and counter through a `morph.updated` hook.
Counter renders `mb_strlen` characters (not bytes) as «۱۲ / ۵۰۰», `dir="ltr"` so current-then-limit reads the same either way, and
is linked from the textarea via `aria-describedby` (not a live region — it would fire on every keystroke).
Disabled applies `inert` + `aria-disabled` to the whole box (action buttons included) and dims the slots.
Focus: the root shows an accent ring via `has-[:focus-visible]`, so typing in the textarea rings the box, a mouse click on
an action button does not.

Livewire contract:
```php
public string $message = '';
public function send() { /* persist $this->message ... */ $this->message = ''; }
```
```blade
<form wire:submit="send">
    <mds:composer wire:model="message" label="پیام" label:sr-only rows="1" max-rows="6" submit="enter" inline
                  placeholder="پیام خود را بنویسید..." name="message">
        <x-slot name="actionsTrailing">
            <flux:button type="submit" size="sm" variant="primary" square><mds:icon icon="paper-airplane" class="size-4" /></flux:button>
        </x-slot>
    </mds:composer>
</form>
```
`wire:model.live` is wasteful here — the default deferred binding sends the text with the submit.

### <mds:color-picker> — color picker (open version of Flux Pro's flux:color-picker)
Props: `value` string|null (any supported color string; normalized to `format`) · `name` · `format` hex|hexa|rgb|rgba|hsl|hsla='hex'
(alpha formats add an alpha slider) · `type` input|button='input' · `label`/`description` (flux:field chrome) · `placeholder` ·
`swatches` array|false|null=20-color default palette (items: hex string or [value, label]) · `dropper` bool=false (EyeDropper API;
auto-hidden if unsupported) · `clearable` bool=false · `size` sm · `disabled` bool=false · `invalid` bool=false ·
`error` string|null (see Validation contract — renders the message) · `fa` bool|null=config (inherited by area/slider/dropper).
wire:model forwarded to hidden input (emits input events). Parses pasted hex(3/6/8-digit)/rgb(a)/hsl(a) strings.
Accessibility: the popover is `role="dialog"` (named by `label`, else «انتخاب رنگ» / "Pick a color"); the trigger has `aria-expanded`,
`aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-controls`; opening moves focus into the panel and closing (Escape / outside click) returns it to
the trigger. `disabled` applies `inert` + `aria-disabled` to the whole control, so nothing inside stays tabbable.
Slot replaces the default popover layout; subcomponents share state:
- `<mds:color-picker.area />` — saturation/brightness canvas, always LTR. Pointer drag on the canvas; keyboard via two visually-hidden
  native `<input type="range">` inside it (`data-mds-color-picker-axis="saturation|brightness"`, labelled «اشباع»/«روشنایی» or
  "Saturation"/"Brightness") wrapped in `role="group"` — two values are not one slider, so it does not claim `role="slider"`. Props: `fa`.
- `<mds:color-picker.slider channel="hue|alpha" />` — native range inputs (keyboard accessible; labelled «رنگ»/«شفافیت» or "Hue"/"Opacity"). Props: `fa`.
- `<mds:color-picker.input placeholder="#000000" />` — parses on change
- `<mds:color-picker.swatches>` + `<mds:color-picker.swatch value="#..." label="..." />`
- `<mds:color-picker.dropper />` — props: `label` (default 'قطره‌چکان' / 'Eyedropper' by fa) · `fa`
RTL note: canvas/sliders stay physically LTR (universal convention); field chrome follows page direction.

### <mds:file-upload> — file upload (open version of Flux Pro's flux:file-upload)
Wrapper. Props: `name` string|null (`[]` auto-appended when `multiple`) · `multiple` bool=false · `accept` string|null (input accept list) ·
`label`/`description` (flux:field chrome) · `error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is set, falls back to
`$errors->first($name)` then `$errors->first("$name.*")`) · `invalid` bool=false · `disabled` bool=false · `fa` bool|null=config.
Renders `flux:field` > `<label>` > sr-only `<input type="file" data-flux-control>` + slot. `wire:model` is forwarded to that input
(everything else lands on the wrapper), so Livewire's native upload pipeline handles the transfer.
Slot = the dropzone, or any custom markup (custom avatar uploader etc.).
Behavior: click anywhere in the slot opens the picker (native `<label>`, so keyboard Enter/Space on the focused input works too);
drag-and-drop writes `input.files` via DataTransfer and dispatches bubbling `change` + `input` (single-file mode keeps only the first drop).
Data attributes on the wrapper: `data-dragging` (file over the zone), `data-loading` (upload in flight) — style descendants with
Tailwind's `in-data-dragging:` / `in-data-loading:` prefixes. Also sets CSS custom properties on the wrapper:
`--mds-file-upload-progress` (Latin `42%`, for widths) and `--mds-file-upload-progress-as-string` (quoted, fa-aware `'۴۲٪'`, for `content:`).

### <mds:file-upload.dropzone>
Props: `heading` string|null (default 'فایل را اینجا رها کنید یا برای انتخاب کلیک کنید', or 'Drop a file here or click to browse' when persian_digits is off) · `text` string|null (size/format hint) ·
`icon` string='cloud-arrow-up' · `inline` bool=false (compact horizontal layout) · `with-progress` bool=false (progress bar + percent
while uploading, replacing `text`; pair it with `text` so the idle state still reads) · `fa` bool|null (inherited from file-upload).
The progress bar is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin/max/now` and `aria-label` «در حال بارگذاری» / "Uploading".
Dashed border, accent border + tint while dragging, accent ring while the input is focus-visible, spinner swap while loading.
Must be rendered inside `<mds:file-upload>` (it reads that component's Alpine state).

### <mds:file-item>
Props: `heading` string|null (file name; `dir="auto"` so Latin names read correctly in RTL lists) · `text` string|null
(defaults to the formatted `size`) · `image` string|null (thumbnail URL) · `size` int|null (bytes -> Persian::fileSize) ·
`icon` string='document' (shown when no `image`) · `invalid` bool=false (red border/icon/text) · `fa` bool|null=config.
Named slot `actions` (inline-end) for buttons; default slot renders under the text column.
Sits OUTSIDE `<mds:file-upload>` — render one per uploaded file yourself (see the Livewire snippet below).

### <mds:file-item.remove>
Props: `icon` string='x-mark' · `label` string|null='حذف فایل' / 'Remove file' by fa (becomes `aria-label`) · `fa` bool|null (inherited from file-item). `wire:click` / `x-on:click` pass through.

Livewire contract (same as Flux):
```php
use Livewire\WithFileUploads; use Livewire\Attributes\Validate;
#[Validate(['photos.*' => 'image|max:10240'])] public $photos = [];
public function removePhoto($i) { $this->photos[$i]->delete(); unset($this->photos[$i]); $this->photos = array_values($this->photos); }
```
```blade
<mds:file-upload wire:model="photos" label="بارگذاری تصاویر" multiple>
    <mds:file-upload.dropzone text="JPG، PNG یا GIF تا ۱۰ مگابایت" with-progress />
</mds:file-upload>
<div class="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-2">
    @foreach ($photos as $i => $photo)
        <mds:file-item :heading="$photo->getClientOriginalName()" :image="$photo->temporaryUrl()" :size="$photo->getSize()">
            <x-slot name="actions"><mds:file-item.remove wire:click="removePhoto({{ $i }})" :label="'حذف '.$photo->getClientOriginalName()" /></x-slot>
        </mds:file-item>
    @endforeach
</div>
```

### <mds:icon> — Hugeicons (replaces heroicons across the kit)
Props: `icon` / `name` string (interchangeable, matching flux:icon) · `variant` string|null (either a Flux variant
`outline|solid|mini|micro` or a Hugeicons style `stroke-rounded|solid-rounded|twotone-rounded|duotone-rounded|
bulk-rounded|stroke-standard|solid-standard|stroke-sharp|solid-sharp`) · `stroke` int|float|null (opt-in
stroke-width override) · `label` string|null (`role="img"` + `aria-label`; without it the icon is `aria-hidden`).
Renders the raw `<svg>` with `data-mds-icon`. Size and colour are plain Tailwind classes (`class="size-4 text-accent"`);
the default 1.5rem comes from mds.css, so any `size-*` utility wins.
Source: the free Stroke Rounded set (6,200 icons) via the `afatmustafa/blade-hugeicons` dependency. Pro styles
resolve only from `mds.icons.sets`.
Resolution order for a name: `Icons::OVERRIDES` -> the literal Hugeicons name -> `Icons::ALIASES` -> `flux:icon`.
So a real Hugeicons name always wins, heroicon names still work, and an unknown name still renders as a heroicon —
unless `mds.icons.strict` is `true`, in which case it renders nothing instead of ever touching `flux:icon`.
`MajidDs\Support\Icons` (static): `ALIASES` (49 heroicon names with no Hugeicons counterpart, e.g.
`magnifying-glass` -> `search-01`, `x-mark` -> `cancel-01`, `cloud-arrow-up` -> `cloud-upload`, `document` -> `file-01`,
`exclamation-triangle` -> `alert-02`, `photo` -> `image-01`, `trash` -> `delete-02`, `users` -> `user-multiple`,
`banknotes` -> `banknote`, `paper-airplane` -> `sent`, `microphone` -> `mic-01`) · `OVERRIDES` (6 names Hugeicons also has but draws differently: `arrow-up|down|left|right`
are chevrons there, `moon` is full not crescent, `map-pin` is a pin on a map) · `STYLES` · `VARIANTS` ·
`FREE_SET` ('hugeicons', the blade-icons set name of the bundled free set) · `PRO_PREFIX` ('mds-hugeicons', Pro sets register as `{PRO_PREFIX}-{style}`) ·
`available(): bool` (a Hugeicons source is registered) · `style(?string $variant): string` · `prefixes(string $style): list<string>` ·
`svg(string $name, ?string $variant, array<string, mixed> $attributes): ?Svg` (attribute values are escaped by `<mds:icon>` before this call — blade-icons does not).
NOTE: `stroke` is opt-in because 478 free icons vary stroke weight on purpose — do not force a global width.
NOTE: `<flux:*>` components (button, badge, navbar, callout, ...) resolve their own `icon` prop internally and keep
rendering heroicons. Only `mds:*` components and `<mds:icon>` use Hugeicons.

### <mds:timeline> — timeline (open version of Flux Pro's flux:timeline)
Container, renders `<ol>`. Props: `horizontal` bool=false (indicators along a row, content beneath) ·
`align` start|baseline|center|end='center' (cross-axis placement of the indicator against its content) · `size` lg|null.
CSS grid: vertical tracks are `[indicator] [content-gap] [content]`; `horizontal` transposes them to rows.
All offsets are logical, so the rail sits on the RIGHT in RTL and a horizontal timeline flows right-to-left.
CSS custom properties (set with an arbitrary class, e.g. `class="[--mds-timeline-item-gap:3rem]"`):
`--mds-timeline-item-gap` (1rem) · `--mds-timeline-content-gap` (0.75rem; 1rem when size=lg) ·
`--mds-timeline-indicator-size` (2rem; 3rem when size=lg) · `--mds-timeline-baseline` (1.25rem, the first
line-height used by `align="baseline"` — this replaces Flux's `[data-flux-timeline-baseline]` font-size trick).

### <mds:timeline.item>
Renders `<li>`. Props: `status` complete|current|incomplete|null · `align` (per-item override; inherited from the
timeline via @aware when omitted) · `size` lg|null (per-item indicator size).
Draws its own leading/trailing connector lines; the first item's leading and the last item's trailing line are
hidden, and a `complete` item paints the rail up to the next indicator in `--color-accent`.
`status="incomplete"` also dims its content to 75%.

### <mds:timeline.indicator>
The dot between the lines — put an icon, a number, or text in the slot. Props: `variant` bare|null
(strips the circle/size so a standalone icon can be the marker) · `status` (overrides the item's) ·
`color` red|orange|amber|yellow|lime|green|emerald|teal|cyan|sky|blue|indigo|violet|purple|fuchsia|pink|rose|zinc|null.
Defaults: zinc chip; `complete` = accent fill, `current` = accent ring, `incomplete` = muted ring.
An explicit `color` outranks `status` (real utility classes beat the layer's defaults).

### <mds:timeline.content>
The cell next to the indicator. No props.

### <mds:timeline.block>
Full-width item body with no indicator column — for callouts, cards, comment threads. Spans every track;
its direct children span the full width unless they are `<mds:timeline.subgrid>`.

### <mds:timeline.subgrid>
Used inside a block to re-align to the timeline's tracks: the first child lands in the indicator track
(centered), every later child in the content track. Vertical timelines only.

Typical order-tracking timeline (Jalali dates, RTL rail):
```blade
<mds:timeline horizontal>
    <mds:timeline.item status="complete">
        <mds:timeline.indicator><flux:icon icon="credit-card" variant="micro" /></mds:timeline.indicator>
        <mds:timeline.content><flux:heading>پرداخت شد</flux:heading><flux:text>@jalali($order->paid_at)</flux:text></mds:timeline.content>
    </mds:timeline.item>
    <mds:timeline.item status="current">
        <mds:timeline.indicator><flux:icon icon="truck" variant="micro" /></mds:timeline.indicator>
        <mds:timeline.content><flux:heading>در حال ارسال</flux:heading></mds:timeline.content>
    </mds:timeline.item>
    <mds:timeline.item status="incomplete">
        <mds:timeline.indicator><flux:icon icon="home" variant="micro" /></mds:timeline.indicator>
        <mds:timeline.content><flux:heading>تحویل به مشتری</flux:heading></mds:timeline.content>
    </mds:timeline.item>
</mds:timeline>
```

### <mds:chart> — monochrome dashboard charts (open alternative to Flux Pro's flux:chart, different API)
Server-rendered SVG/HTML in the Mono Charts style (Amicro, MIT) — no chart library, no script, no wire:model.
The card chrome; the `mds:chart.*` stages below draw the charts and also work standalone anywhere.
Props: `label` string (uppercase kicker) · `badge` string (pill next to it) · `value` int|float|string (big stat;
numbers get separators, strings keep their shape with localized digits) · `unit` string (faint suffix) ·
`delta` string (change readout — green, red when it starts with `-`) · `footer-start`/`footer-end` string ·
`fa` bool|null=config (inherited by the stages inside via @aware — see `fa` inheritance).
Accessibility: every SVG stage is `role="img"` with a bilingual `aria-label` — bars/line/radar name the chart type («نمودار ستونی» /
"Bar chart"…); donut and gauge fold `label` + the value into the name because `role="img"` makes the SVG's own text presentational.
sparkline is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
Slots: `header` (trailing side of the header row) · `footer` (replaces the footer props) · default (the stages).
Ink contract: every stage's ink is currentColor at fixed opacity steps — `class="text-accent"` on a stage
recolors the whole chart. Direction contract: the SVG plot plane is always LTR (like the color-picker canvas);
the HTML stages — bullet, heatmap, horizontal bars — follow the page direction, so funnels grow rightward in RTL.

### <mds:chart.line> — rounded spline (SVG)
Props: `data` number[] · `labels` string[] (x categories) · `baseline` number[] (dashed faint twin series, same
axis) · `area` bool=false (gradient under the curve) · `dots` bool=true (stage-halo point markers) ·
`curve` smooth|straight='smooth' (smooth = monotone cubic, never overshoots) · `axis` bool=true (Persian-digit
y ticks on a "nice" 0..ceiling scale, dashed grid, x labels) · `max` number|null (pins the ceiling) ·
`width` int=360 / `height` int=170 (viewBox; scales to its box) · `fa`.

### <mds:chart.bars> — pill bars (SVG), or direction-aware rows
Props: `data` (number|number[])[] — an array item stacks: solid base then lighter tones up, only the stack's
outer ends rounded · `secondary` number[] (faint twin next to each bar) · `labels` string[] ·
`horizontal` bool=false — switches to HTML label/track/value rows (the funnel layout; follows page direction) ·
`axis` bool=true · `max` · `width`/`height` · `fa`.

### <mds:chart.donut> — rounded ring (SVG)
Props: `data` array<label, number> · `value` (center readout; default: the sum) · `label` (under it) ·
`legend` bool=true (tone-matched dots + labels) · `size` int=160 · `thickness` int=22 · `fa`.
Segments are stroked arcs with round caps and real gaps, shaded down a fixed tone ladder (1/.7/.4/.2) in order;
very thin segments (< ~8% of the ring) collapse to a dot.

### <mds:chart.gauge> — 240° dial (SVG)
Props: `value` number · `max` number=100 · `label` (under the readout) · `decimals` int=0 · `fa`.

### <mds:chart.radar> — polygon web (SVG)
Props: `data` array<label, number> · `max` number=100 · `fa`. Four grid rings, one spoke per key, first axis
at 12 o'clock; the shape fills at 15% ink.

### <mds:chart.bullet> — value-vs-target rows (HTML, RTL-native)
Props: `items` array of ['label' => string, 'value' => number, 'target' => number|null] · `max` number=100 ·
`unit` string='%' · `fa`. The target marker is the family's one accent: it sits on `--color-accent`.

### <mds:chart.heatmap> — activity grid (HTML, RTL-native)
Props: `data` number[] (column-major: every `rows` values are one column/week) · `rows` int=7 ·
`labels` string[] (spread across the top) · `color` accent|null (tone ladder base; default the ink) ·
`unit` string|null='مورد' / 'items' by fa · `callout` bool=true (readout row under the grid, `aria-live="polite"`; cells keep a
`title` fallback without Alpine) · `fa`. Values grade into 5 tones of the base via color-mix.
Keyboard: the grid is ONE tab stop (roving tabindex — a year of cells is not 365 stops); Arrow Up/Down walk a column, Left/Right jump
columns and mirror in RTL. Each cell is `role="img"` with `aria-label` «۳ مورد» / "3 items"; focus and hover both update the callout.

### <mds:chart.sparkline> — bare inline spline (SVG)
Props: `data` number[] (auto-fits its own range — shape, not scale) · `area` bool=false ·
`curve` smooth|straight='smooth' · `width` int=120 / `height` int=28.
A bare <svg> with preserveAspectRatio=none + non-scaling 2px stroke: size it with any width/height utilities.
No fa (it renders no text). KPI card recipe = mds:chart with `delta` + a sparkline, no stage box:
```blade
<mds:chart label="درآمد ماهانه" :value="48920" unit="هزار تومان" delta="+14.2%">
    <mds:chart.sparkline :data="[30, 45, 35, 60, 50, 85, 75, 95]" area class="h-16" />
</mds:chart>
```

### <mds:popover> — a panel anchored to its trigger (open version of Flux Pro's flux:popover)
Compound: `<mds:popover>` (root, holds the state) + `<mds:popover.trigger>` + `<mds:popover.content>`.
Root props: `position` top|bottom|start|end='bottom' (logical: start/end resolve against the component's own direction, so
placement mirrors on RTL pages — and inside RTL islands on an LTR page) · `align` start|center|end='start' (alignment along
that side; `start` hugs the leading edge, which is the trigger's right edge in RTL) · `offset` int=8 (px gap from the trigger;
cast to an int, and negatives clamp to 0) · `arrow` bool=false (inherited by the content) · `hover` bool=false (open on hover and
on keyboard focus as well as on click) · `fa` bool|null=config (picks the close button's language; inherited by the content).
An unknown `position` or `align` falls back to the default instead of producing a broken placement.
- `<mds:popover.trigger>` — no props. Wrap exactly ONE focusable element (a `flux:button`, a link, an input). Blade cannot
  inject attributes into slot content, so the click handler lives on this `<span>` (`[data-mds-popover-trigger]`) and the ARIA
  state is written onto the real button at runtime, where a screen reader reads it. With no focusable child the wrapper itself
  is used, and the popover is then mouse-only — don't do that.
- `<mds:popover.content>` props: `arrow` bool|null (inherited from the root; set it here to override one panel) · `closable`
  bool=false (adds a corner close button labelled «بستن» / "Close" by `fa`, and reserves room for it with `pe-10`) ·
  `fa` bool|null (inherited from the root). Size and padding are yours — `class="w-72"`, `class="!p-0"`; the default look is
  the kit's dropdown surface (`min-w-48`, rounded, bordered, `p-4`, `text-start`).
Behavior (Alpine): the panel is wrapped in `<template x-teleport="body">` — the template keeps a block-level panel legal inside
a `<p>` and teleports it out of `overflow-hidden` and transformed ancestors. It is `position: fixed`, placed from measured
rects on open, flipped to the opposite side when the preferred one has no room and the other does, clamped to the viewport
(5px padding), and repositioned on scroll (capturing) and resize while open — those listeners are attached on open, dropped on
close and in `destroy()`. The chosen side is written to `data-rendered-side` on the panel, and the arrow (a rotated square
borrowing the panel's border) follows it and points at the middle of the trigger. The open/close transition is opacity only
and is skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Clicking the trigger toggles and *pins* the popover; Escape (window-level), a click outside, or the close button closes it.
Opening by click or keyboard moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the panel; closing returns it to the trigger
when focus was still inside. The panel is non-modal, so focus is not trapped: Tab off its last control closes it and continues
at the element after the trigger, Shift+Tab off its first closes it and returns to the trigger.
`hover` adds an open delay of 100ms and a close delay of 300ms, so the panel neither flickers under a passing cursor nor
vanishes on the way to it; keyboard focus (`:focus-visible` only) opens it immediately, and a click pins it so the mouse
leaving no longer closes it.
Events: the root dispatches bubbling `mds-popover-open` and `mds-popover-close` CustomEvents — listen on the tag itself
(`x-on:mds-popover-close="…"`, `@mds-popover-open.window="…"`). The Alpine component's `toggle()`, `show()` and `close()` are
public.
ARIA contract: the panel is `role="dialog"` `aria-modal="false"` `tabindex="-1"`, named by its trigger through
`aria-labelledby` unless the caller passes its own `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` (either one suppresses the automatic
link). At runtime the real trigger button gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the
panel — a generic wrapper `<span>` never carries them. Markers for tests and CSS: `data-mds-popover` (root),
`data-mds-popover-trigger`, `data-mds-popover-content`, `data-mds-popover-close`, `data-mds-popover-arrow`.
Livewire contract: the popover holds no value, so there is no `wire:model`. Every attribute lands on the root, so
`x-on:mds-popover-close="$wire.save()"` and `wire:key` work as usual; `wire:click` on buttons inside the content is ordinary
markup. One caveat comes with the teleport: Alpine moves the panel out of the Livewire component's DOM and into `<body>` as
soon as it initialises (it is always there, hidden by `x-show`, not created on open), and Livewire's morph follows teleported
nodes — the same mechanism `<mds:preview-card>` already relies on.
```blade
<mds:popover position="bottom" align="end" arrow>
    <mds:popover.trigger>
        <flux:button icon="bell" variant="ghost">اعلان‌ها</flux:button>
    </mds:popover.trigger>

    <mds:popover.content closable class="w-72">
        <flux:heading size="sm">اعلان‌ها</flux:heading>
        <flux:text class="mt-2">سفارش شما ارسال شد و سه‌شنبه به دستتان می‌رسد.</flux:text>
        <flux:separator class="my-3" />
        <flux:link href="/notifications">مشاهده همه اعلان‌ها</flux:link>
    </mds:popover.content>
</mds:popover>
```

### <mds:accordion> — collapsible sections (open version of Flux Pro's flux:accordion)
Compound: `<mds:accordion>` (the group) + `<mds:accordion.item>` + `<mds:accordion.heading>` + `<mds:accordion.content>`.
Every item is a native `<details>`/`<summary>` pair, so opening, closing, Enter/Space, focus and find-in-page come from the
browser and work with JavaScript off.
Root props: `exclusive` bool=false (only one item open at a time) · `transition` bool=false (animate the open/close height) ·
`name` string|null (explicit group name for the `<details name>` attribute; only used when `exclusive`) · `fa` bool|null=config
(no digits and no microcopy of its own — accepted for parity and handed down to the parts).
- `<mds:accordion.item>` props: `expanded` bool=false (renders the `open` attribute, so the first paint is right) ·
  `disabled` bool=false (not focusable, not toggleable) · `heading` string|null (shortcut: renders
  `<mds:accordion.heading>` + `<mds:accordion.content>` around the slot, escaped — pass the subcomponents instead when the
  heading needs markup) · `fa` bool|null. Renders the `<details>`; carries `data-expanded` / `data-disabled`.
- `<mds:accordion.heading>` props: `fa` bool|null. The `<summary>`: `role="button"`, the caller's text in a
  `min-w-0 flex-1` span, and a chevron that rotates 180° when open. Inherits `expanded`/`disabled` from the item.
- `<mds:accordion.content>` props: `fa` bool|null. The body. Its padding sits on an inner `pb-4` box so the height
  animation can run the outer element down to zero.
Behavior (Alpine): Alpine only adds what `<details>` lacks. `disabled` cancels the summary's click (and drops it from the tab
order). `exclusive` uses the native `<details name>` group — the server writes the shared constant `mds-accordion` when no
`name` was given (so the group works before any script runs; two unnamed accordions on one page act as one group for that
instant) and each item swaps in a per-accordion `$id()` at init. With `transition` the `name` attribute is removed instead and
the siblings are closed by script, animated: a Web Animations height tween of 200ms `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`, run on the
content and skipped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion` (the item then toggles natively). Re-opening mid-collapse grows
back from wherever the box is. A nested accordion keeps its own group. Markers for tests and CSS: `data-mds-accordion`
(+ `data-mds-accordion-exclusive`, `data-mds-accordion-name`, `data-mds-accordion-transition`), `data-mds-accordion-item`,
`data-mds-accordion-heading`, `data-mds-accordion-content`, `data-mds-accordion-chevron`.
ARIA contract: the `<summary>` is the button — `role="button"` with `aria-expanded` rendered server-side from `expanded` and
kept in step by Alpine; a disabled item's summary is `aria-disabled="true"` `tabindex="-1"` `pointer-events-none`. The chevron
is `aria-hidden`. Keyboard: Tab reaches each heading, Enter and Space toggle it — the native `<details>` behaviour. This is the
WAI-ARIA accordion pattern's required set; the optional Up/Down/Home/End roving between headings is deliberately not
implemented, because it would mean taking the summary's native semantics away.
Livewire contract: no `wire:model` — the accordion holds no value. `wire:click` and `x-on:click` on a heading pass through, and
attributes land on each part's own root, so `wire:key` belongs on `<mds:accordion.item>` in a loop. A morph that changes the
`open` attribute fires the native `toggle` event and Alpine re-reads it (`this.expanded = this.$el.open` at init as well), so a
server-driven `expanded` stays in sync. Style descendants off the state with `in-data-expanded:` /
`group-open/mds-accordion:` — the item is `group/mds-accordion`.
```blade
<mds:accordion exclusive transition class="max-w-lg">
    <mds:accordion.item expanded>
        <mds:accordion.heading>ارسال و تحویل</mds:accordion.heading>
        <mds:accordion.content>سفارش‌ها حداکثر تا دو روز کاری ارسال می‌شوند.</mds:accordion.content>
    </mds:accordion.item>

    <mds:accordion.item heading="مرجوع کردن کالا">تا هفت روز، بدون پرسش.</mds:accordion.item>
    <mds:accordion.item heading="گارانتی" disabled>به‌زودی</mds:accordion.item>
</mds:accordion>
```

### <mds:slider> — range slider (open version of Flux Pro's flux:slider)
Native `<input type="range">` controls under kit styling: one thumb, or two that hold a range. Props: `value` int|float|array|null=`min`
(a range takes `[low, high]`; a single slider takes a number) · `min` numeric=0 · `max` numeric=100 (an inverted pair is swapped) ·
`step` numeric=1 (fractions welcome; anything `<= 0` falls back to 1) · `range` bool=false (two thumbs that may not cross) ·
`label` / `description` (flux:label + flux:description chrome; the label also names the thumbs) · `name` string|null (plain form post —
a range posts as `name[]` — and the key the error bag is read with) · `size` sm|null · `disabled` bool=false ·
`show-value` bool=false (live readout beside the label) · `ticks` bool|int=false (`true` draws one tick per step while the span divides
into at most 20 whole steps, and nothing when it would crowd the track; an int draws that many, evenly spaced) ·
`format` string|null (a `{value}` template applied to the readout and `aria-valuetext`, e.g. `{value} تومان` or `{value}٪`) ·
`invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is set, falls back to `$errors->first($name)`,
then — for a range — `$errors->first($name.'.*')`) · `fa` bool|null=config (digits of the readout and language of the built-in labels).
Behavior: values are clamped to the bounds and snapped to the step grid on the SERVER too, so the first paint, a no-JS form post and the
thumb all agree. Alpine mirrors the native inputs (it never writes `value` back into them), keeps `low <= high` by pushing a crossing
thumb back and re-announcing the clamped value in the same tick, and — in range mode only — moves the nearer thumb to a press on the bare
track. The fill between the thumbs is two CSS custom properties (`--mds-slider-a` / `--mds-slider-b`) set server-side and kept up to date
by Alpine, so it is painted before Alpine boots. Keyboard is the browser's own: arrows step, PageUp/PageDown jump, Home/End go to the
bounds, and the arrows follow the visual direction in RTL because the native control already does.
ARIA contract: each thumb is a real `input[type=range]`, so `role="slider"`, `aria-valuemin/max/now` and the keyboard come free. The kit adds
`aria-label` — the `label` text, or «مقدار» / "Value" — suffixed with « — حداقل» / " — minimum" and « — حداکثر» / " — maximum" on a range,
`aria-valuetext` (the formatted, `fa`-aware reading, kept in sync by Alpine), `aria-invalid` on every thumb when invalid, and
`aria-describedby` pointing at the description and the error message. The readout is an `aria-live="polite"` region; the track, fill and
ticks are `aria-hidden`. Ticks are decoration — they never replace `step`.
Data hooks: `data-mds-slider` on the root (plus `data-mds-slider-range`, `data-mds-slider-size="sm"`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`),
`data-mds-slider-header`, `-value`, `-track`, `-fill`, `-ticks`, `-tick`, and `data-mds-slider-input="value|low|high"` on the controls.
Livewire contract: `wire:model` is forwarded to the native input(s) and the wrapper keeps no copy. A single slider binds the property as
written. A RANGE binds the two ends as dotted paths, keeping the caller's modifiers: `wire:model.live="price"` becomes
`wire:model.live="price.0"` on the low thumb and `wire:model.live="price.1"` on the high one — so the bound property must be an ARRAY of
two numbers (`public array $price = [500000, 3000000];`), never a scalar. A server-side change of the property flows back through the
`x-model` accessor Livewire leaves on the input, so the readout and the fill follow a `$this->price = [...]` from a Livewire action.
```blade
<mds:slider wire:model.live="price" range name="price" label="بازه قیمت" :min="0" :max="5000000" :step="250000"
            :value="$price" format="{value} تومان" show-value description="قیمت‌ها به تومان است." />
```
```php
public array $price = [500000, 3000000];   // price.0 and price.1 — a scalar would break the binding
public function updatedPrice() { $this->resetPage(); }
```

### <mds:time-picker> — time field with a list of times (open version of Flux Pro's flux:time-picker)
A typable combobox over a server-rendered list of times. The visible field shows «۱۴:۳۰» or "2:30 PM"; a hidden input carries the
machine value, always 24-hour `HH:MM` with Latin digits. Props: `value` string|null (`HH:MM`, `H:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`, Persian/Arabic digits
accepted; normalized to `HH:MM`, and anything that is not a time renders empty) · `name` string|null (plain form post, and the key the error
bag is read with — it lands on the hidden input alone) · `label` / `description` (flux:field chrome; `label` also names the listbox) ·
`placeholder` string='--:--' · `step` int=30 (minutes between listed times; `<= 0` falls back to 1) · `min` string|null='00:00' ·
`max` string|null='23:59' (both as `HH:MM`; the list runs from `min` to `max` inclusive, and a `max` the step skips is simply not listed) ·
`hours` 12|24=24 (display only — the machine value stays 24-hour) · `clearable` bool=false (a clear button that shows once there is a value) ·
`disabled` bool=false (`inert` + `aria-disabled` on the whole control) · `size` sm|null · `icon` string|false='clock' (leading `mds:icon`;
`false` removes it) · `invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is set, falls back to
`$errors->first($name)`) · `fa` bool|null=config (digits, the AM/PM words «ق.ظ»/«ب.ظ» vs "AM"/"PM", and the clear button's label).
Behavior: the field is typable as well as pickable. Typing accepts `1430`, `14:30`, `2:30 pm`, `۱۴:۳۰`, `۲:۳۰ ب.ظ` and the same with Arabic
digits or a `.`/`،`/`-`/space separator; a bare number without an AM/PM word reads as a 24-hour time; «صبح/قبل/ق.ظ» and «عصر/شب/بعد/ب.ظ»
are understood alongside am/pm. The typed minute is kept as typed (it is NOT rounded to `step`) and clamped to `min`/`max`; text that is not
a time reverts to the last valid value on Enter or blur. With the list open the arrows preview an option in the field and Enter commits it;
with the list closed the arrows nudge the value itself by `step` (Flux's behaviour). Home/End jump to the first/last option, Alt+ArrowDown /
Alt+ArrowUp open and close the list, Escape reverts and closes, Tab closes, and a click outside commits what is typed. Opening with no value
scrolls the list to the option nearest the current clock time. The list and the field are always `dir="ltr"` (a time reads
hour-then-minute in both languages) and end-aligned in an RTL form.
ARIA contract: the visible input is `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`,
`aria-controls` -> the listbox and `aria-activedescendant` -> the previewed option; option ids come from Alpine's `$id()`, so two pickers on a
page never share one. Options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`, inside a `role="listbox"` named by `label`. The error message is
`role="alert"`; `aria-invalid` marks the field. `inputmode="numeric"` is requested in 24-hour mode only — typing "pm" needs letters.
Data hooks: `data-mds-time-picker` (root, plus `data-disabled`), `-control`, `-input`, `-clear`, `-listbox`, `-option` (each carrying
`data-value="HH:MM"`).
Livewire contract: `wire:model` is forwarded to the hidden input and nowhere else; the wrapper keeps no copy. The bound property is a
`HH:MM` string (`''` when cleared), which `date_format:H:i` validates and Carbon parses directly. Every Alpine change writes the hidden
input and dispatches a bubbling `input` event, and a `MutationObserver` on the hidden input's `value` attribute pulls a server-side change
back into the field, so `$this->at = '09:00'` in an action re-renders the display text too.
```blade
<mds:time-picker wire:model.live="at" name="at" label="ساعت تحویل" description="بازه‌های نیم‌ساعته."
                 :value="$at" min="09:00" max="21:00" :step="30" clearable />
```
```php
public string $at = '10:30';
protected function rules() { return ['at' => 'required|date_format:H:i']; }
```

### <mds:tabs> — the tab list (open version of Flux Pro's flux:tabs)
Props: `variant` default|segmented|pills='default' (an unknown value falls back to default) · `size` sm|null=null
(`sm` shrinks every tab in the list) · `label` string|null — the tablist's accessible name, default «زبانه‌ها» / "Tabs" by fa ·
`name` string|null (posts the active tab under that name in a plain form) · `fa` bool|null=config (inherited from the group).
Renders the `role="tablist"` `aria-orientation="horizontal"` element plus the hidden control Livewire binds to
(`<input type="hidden" data-mds-tabs-input>`); `wire:model*` written on `<mds:tabs>` is forwarded to that input and is never
left on the list. The list scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping (its scrollbar is hidden), so a long row of tabs stays one row.
Markers: `data-mds-tabs`, `data-mds-tabs-variant`, `data-mds-tabs-size`. The active tab is inherited from the enclosing
`<mds:tab.group>` — the list never decides on its own, it only resolves the group's `value` against the tabs it actually holds.

### <mds:tab> — one tab, its group and its panels (open version of Flux Pro's flux:tab)
Props: `name` string, REQUIRED — pairs the tab with the `<mds:tab.panel>` of the same name; a missing name throws
InvalidArgumentException · `icon` heroicon name|null (leading, rendered through `<mds:icon variant="micro">`) ·
`icon-trailing` heroicon name|null — Flux's `icon:trailing` spelling is accepted too and is consumed, not printed ·
`disabled` bool=false (a real disabled `<button>`: skipped by the arrow keys and never chosen as the default) ·
`fa` bool|null=config (accepted for symmetry; a tab has no built-in text of its own).
Renders `<button type="button" role="tab" id="mds-tab-{slug}" aria-controls="mds-tabpanel-{slug}">` where `{slug}` is the
name with every run of non-letter/non-digit characters replaced by `-` — Persian names survive intact. Marker `data-mds-tab="{name}"`.
Compose:
- `<mds:tab.group>` props: `value` string|null — the tab shown first; when it names a disabled or unknown tab the first ENABLED tab wins instead · `fa` bool|null=config (inherited by the list, the tabs and the panels). Holds the Alpine state (`Alpine.data('mdsTabs')`, registered once per page behind a started-Alpine guard) and wraps list + panels. Marker `data-mds-tab-group`. Groups nest: a group inside a panel keeps its own state and its own default.
- `<mds:tab.panel>` props: `name` string, REQUIRED — the tab it belongs to; a missing name throws InvalidArgumentException · `fa` bool|null=config. Renders `role="tabpanel"` `tabindex="0"` `id="mds-tabpanel-{slug}"` `aria-labelledby="mds-tab-{slug}"`, `hidden` on the server unless it is the active one. Marker `data-mds-tab-panel="{name}"`.
Behavior: the first ENABLED tab is active when the group has no `value`, and the server resolves that before Alpine runs — the right
panel is visible in the very first paint, and with JavaScript off the page is still correct (only switching needs Alpine). Clicking a
tab selects it; the panels are toggled by `hidden`, so all of them stay in the DOM and keep their form state.
ARIA contract: the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern with AUTOMATIC activation. Roving tabindex — the active tab is the only tab stop
(`tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`) and carries `aria-selected="true"` plus `data-selected` (styling hooks off the attribute, never off a
colour alone). ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move focus AND select, wrapping at both ends and skipping disabled tabs; Home/End jump to the
first/last enabled tab. Left/Right follow the VISUAL order: `getComputedStyle(tablist).direction` is read at keydown, so an RTL island
in an LTR page moves the way it looks. Panels are focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so a keyboard user can reach panel content that has no
control of its own.
Livewire contract: `wire:model` / `wire:model.live` on `<mds:tabs>` binds the active tab's NAME (a plain string) through the hidden
input, which dispatches a bubbling `input` event on every user selection. A morph that changes the bound property rewrites that input's
`value` attribute; a MutationObserver (`attributeFilter: ['value']`, disconnected in `destroy()`) re-reads it into Alpine, and a value
that names no enabled tab is quietly corrected to the first one without dispatching an event. Flux puts the binding on the GROUP;
here it belongs on the list, and `wire:model` written on `<mds:tab.group>` throws InvalidArgumentException rather than landing on a
plain div where Livewire would ignore it. Other `wire:*` attributes on the group pass through untouched.
```blade
<mds:tab.group value="specs">
    <mds:tabs variant="segmented" label="بخش‌های محصول" wire:model.live="tab">
        <mds:tab name="specs" icon="document-text">مشخصات</mds:tab>
        <mds:tab name="reviews" icon="star">نظرات</mds:tab>
        <mds:tab name="qna" icon="chat-bubble-left-right" disabled>پرسش و پاسخ</mds:tab>
    </mds:tabs>

    <mds:tab.panel name="specs">…</mds:tab.panel>
    <mds:tab.panel name="reviews">…</mds:tab.panel>
    <mds:tab.panel name="qna">…</mds:tab.panel>
</mds:tab.group>
```

### <mds:autocomplete> — text input with a suggestion list (open version of Flux Pro's flux:autocomplete)
A `flux:input` that keeps its free text and offers matching options underneath: type-ahead, not a select. Props: `value`
string|null (initial text) · `name` string|null (plain form post + the key `$errors` is read with; defaults to the
`wire:model` expression, exactly as flux:input does) · `label` / `description` (flux:field chrome; `label` also names the
listbox) · `placeholder` string|null · `icon` string|null (leading icon, passed to flux:input) · `clearable` bool=false
(trailing × button, hidden while the field is empty) · `min-chars` int=0 (characters needed before the list opens) ·
`empty` bool|string|null=false (the no-match line: absent the list just hides, a bare `empty` uses the built-in
'موردی یافت نشد.' / 'No matches.', a string is shown as given) · `strict` bool=false (on blur, snap the text to a matching
option's own spelling, or clear it when it matches none) · `disabled` bool=false · `size` sm|xs|null (flux:input size) ·
`error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is set, falls back to `$errors->first($name)`) ·
`invalid` bool=false (any error implies it) · `fa` bool|null=config (picks the language of the built-in strings; inherited
by items). `wire:model` is forwarded to the text input; everything else lands on the root `[data-mds-autocomplete]` div.
- `<mds:autocomplete.item>` props: `value` string|null (what is written into the input when picked; the item's own text
  when absent) · `disabled` bool=false (stays visible, greyed, skipped by the cursor and unclickable) · `fa` bool|null
  (inherited). Default slot = the option's label. Attributes land on the option. Renders `role="option"` inside the
  listbox with `data-mds-autocomplete-item` and a `[data-mds-autocomplete-label]` span the highlighter rewrites.
Behavior (Alpine `mdsAutocomplete`): WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup — *list autocomplete with manual selection*,
so typing filters but selects nothing; the arrow keys move a virtual cursor and Enter or a click copies that option's
value into the input. Matching is substring on the option's text after Persian normalization (Arabic ي/ى/ك fold to ی/ک,
Persian and Arabic-Indic digits fold to Latin), so typing 'كتاب' or '٢' still matches; the matched run of every visible
label is wrapped in a `<mark>` built from text nodes, so typed text never reaches innerHTML. Keys: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move
and wrap (from nothing active, Down takes the first option and Up the last, and either opens a closed list), Home/End jump
to the ends, Enter picks the active option, Escape closes, Tab closes and moves on. Enter, Escape, Home and End only act
while the list is open — a closed autocomplete is an ordinary text field, so Enter submits its form. The list opens on
focus and closes on blur; the popup prevents `mousedown`, so clicking an option (or dragging its scrollbar) never blurs
the input. `min-chars` holds the list shut until enough is typed. The option cache follows the DOM: a MutationObserver on
the root re-scans (collapsed to one pass per microtask) when a Livewire morph or an `x-for` adds, removes or relabels
items, keeping the cursor on the same option where it survives — so server-side search works. The observer and its
records are cleared in `destroy()`.
ARIA contract: the input is `role="combobox"` `aria-autocomplete="list"` `autocomplete="off"` with `aria-expanded`
tracking the popup, `aria-controls` → the listbox and `aria-activedescendant` → the active option (ids assigned at init
from Alpine's `$id`). Options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected` on the active one and `aria-disabled="true"` on
disabled ones; they are never in the tab order — focus stays in the input. The no-match line is a `role="status"` region
OUTSIDE the listbox (a listbox takes options, not prose). The clear button is labelled 'پاک کردن' / 'Clear'. The error is
the `flux:error` markup (`role="alert"`), rendered without its dependency on the session bag. CSS hooks:
`[data-mds-autocomplete]`, `-input`, `-clear`, `-popup`, `-list`, `-item`, `-label`, `-empty`; `[data-disabled]` on the
root and on disabled options.
Livewire contract: the bound property holds the *text*, not an id — `wire:model.live` is the useful mode when the options
are queried on the server.
```php
public string $city = '';
public function getCitiesProperty() { return City::where('name', 'like', "%{$this->city}%")->take(8)->get(); }
```
```blade
<mds:autocomplete wire:model.live.debounce.300ms="city" name="city" label="شهر" placeholder="نام شهر را بنویسید..."
                  icon="map-pin" clearable :min-chars="2" empty strict>
    @foreach ($this->cities as $city)
        <mds:autocomplete.item :value="$city->name">{{ $city->name }}</mds:autocomplete.item>
    @endforeach
</mds:autocomplete>
```

### <mds:carousel> — slide strip with controls, dots and autoplay (open version of Flux Pro's flux:carousel)
A CSS scroll-snap track (`snap-x snap-mandatory`, scrollbar hidden): native swiping on touch and trackpads, and RTL for
free — the strip scrolls the other way with no direction arithmetic. Props: `label` string|null (the region's
`aria-label`; default 'اسلایدشو', or 'Slideshow' by fa) · `autoplay` bool=false · `interval` int=5000 (ms between slides,
floor 500) · `loop` bool=true (after the last position comes the first; `false` disables the edge buttons and stops
autoplay at the end) · `indicators` bool=true (one dot per start position) · `controls` bool=true (previous/next
buttons) · `per-view` int=1 (slides visible at once; sets `--mds-carousel-per-view` on the track, and each item is
`flex: 0 0 calc((100% - (n - 1) * gap) / n)`) · `gap` string|null (a Tailwind gap class for the track, default `gap-0`;
the length is derived from the class name for the first paint — `gap-4`, `gap-x-4`, `gap-px`, `gap-[10px]` — published as
`--mds-carousel-gap` and corrected from the computed style at init) · `start` int=0 (initial position, clamped to the
last one) · `aspect` string|null (an aspect-ratio class for the track, e.g. `aspect-video`; slot content then sizes with
`h-full w-full object-cover`) · `fa` bool|null=config (picks the language of the built-in strings and the digits;
inherited by items). Everything else lands on the root `[data-mds-carousel]` div; there is no `wire:model`.
- `<mds:carousel.item>` props: `fa` bool|null (inherited). Default slot = any content (an image, an mds:product-card).
  Renders `role="group" aria-roledescription="اسلاید"/"slide"`; Alpine writes `aria-label` «{n} از {total}» / "{n} of
  {total}" at init, since a slot cannot know its own position. Attributes land on the item.
Behavior (Alpine `mdsCarousel`): the active slide is the first one at least 60% inside the track
(IntersectionObserver rooted on the track), so swipes, trackpad scrolls, buttons, dots and keys all agree. `go(i)` calls
`scrollIntoView({ inline: 'start' })` — smooth, or instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`. With `per-view` n and N slides
there are N - n + 1 positions; the dots, `loop` and End all count positions, not slides. A MutationObserver on the track
re-scans when a Livewire morph or an `x-for` adds or removes slides (only direct children, so a nested carousel keeps its
own); the dots are server-rendered and follow a Livewire re-render. Keyboard, on the whole region: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight
follow the VISUAL order (`getComputedStyle().direction` read at keydown, so Right is «previous» in RTL), Home/End jump to
the edges; a modifier key, or a text field / contenteditable inside a slide, keeps its own arrows. Autoplay is one
`setInterval`, and a tick is skipped while the pointer is over the carousel, focus is inside it, a swipe is still
settling or the tab is hidden; `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` starts it paused (the play button still works) and
switching the preference on mid-show pauses it. A pause/play button appears only with `autoplay`; its label switches
between 'توقف'/'Pause' and 'پخش'/'Play' (a changing label, so no `aria-pressed`). Intervals, timeouts, both observers and
the media-query listener are cleared in `destroy()`.
ARIA contract: root `role="region" aria-roledescription="اسلایدشو"/"carousel" aria-label`; the track is a focusable
scroller (`tabindex="0"`) whose id the buttons point at with `aria-controls` (runtime `$id`); previous/next buttons are
labelled 'قبلی'/'Previous' and 'بعدی'/'Next', sit at inline-start/inline-end in both directions and show the chevron that
points that way (`rtl:hidden`/`ltr:hidden`), disabled at the ends when `loop` is off; dots are buttons labelled
'رفتن به اسلاید {n}'/'Go to slide {n}' with `aria-current="true"` on the active one; a visually hidden live region
announces «اسلاید ۲ از ۵» / "Slide 2 of 5" when the USER moves, and is `aria-live="off"` while auto-rotating (WAI-ARIA
carousel guidance — a region that speaks every few seconds is noise). CSS hooks: `[data-mds-carousel]`, `-track`,
`-item`, `-prev`, `-next`, `-toggle`, `-indicators`, `-dot`, `-status`.
```blade
<mds:carousel label="محصولات ویژه" aspect="aspect-video" autoplay :interval="4000">
    <mds:carousel.item><img src="/banners/1.jpg" alt="جشنواره پاییزه" class="h-full w-full object-cover"></mds:carousel.item>
    <mds:carousel.item><img src="/banners/2.jpg" alt="ارسال رایگان" class="h-full w-full object-cover"></mds:carousel.item>
</mds:carousel>

<mds:carousel per-view="3" gap="gap-4" :loop="false" :indicators="false" :start="0">
    @foreach ($products as $product)
        <mds:carousel.item><mds:product-card :title="$product->title" :amount="$product->price" /></mds:carousel.item>
    @endforeach
</mds:carousel>
```

### <mds:context> — right-click menu around any content (open version of Flux Pro's flux:context)
Wraps a card, a row, an image — anything — and shows a menu at the pointer on right-click. The menu is the caller's own
free-tier `<flux:menu>`, so items, separators, checkboxes, radios and submenus are Flux's, unchanged.
Props: `disabled` bool=false (renders no handlers at all; the native menu comes back) · `long-press` bool=true (on touch, a
500ms press opens the menu; moving 10px, lifting or scrolling first cancels it; `false` disables the touch path) ·
`focusable` bool=false (adds `tabindex="0"` to the wrapper — ONLY for content with no focusable element of its own, so
keyboard users have somewhere to press Shift+F10; content with buttons/links needs nothing) · `fa` bool|null=config
(inherited by the menu; there are no built-in strings today, so it is a contract, not a switch).
Slot: the content the menu belongs to, followed by the menu subcomponent. Attributes land on the root `[data-mds-context]`
div (`class` merges with `relative`).
- `<mds:context.menu>` props: `fa`. The panel: `<template x-teleport="body">` around a `fixed z-50` div `[data-mds-context-menu]`
  (`x-show="open"`, `x-cloak`; `class` merges). Its slot is the `<flux:menu>…</flux:menu>`. Teleported, so it inherits the PAGE's
  `dir` and a block panel is legal inside a `<p>` or a `<span>`.
Behavior (Alpine `mdsContext`, state `open`/`x`/`y`): opens on `contextmenu` (preventDefault; positioned at the pointer), on the
keyboard's ContextMenu key or Shift+F10 while focus is inside (positioned at the focused element's bottom-start corner), and on a
touch long-press. Position is physical viewport pixels on purpose — the anchor is a pointer, not an element: the menu's START edge
sits at the pointer (left edge on LTR pages, right edge on RTL, like native menus), flips to the other side of the pointer when out
