of room, flips above it near the bottom, then clamps to the viewport (4px). Closes on Escape, Tab, a click/tap outside (pointerdown,
capture), a click on an item (Flux's `lofi-close-popovers` or any button/link in a custom slot), window blur and any scroll
(capture); repositions on resize. Focus returns to the element that had it. Flux renders `<flux:menu>` as a `popover="manual"`
element (hidden until shown), so the component drives the popover API: `showPopover()` on open puts the menu in the TOP LAYER —
above Flux modals (`<dialog>`) and every clipping ancestor — and the menu element itself is positioned there. A slot that is not a
popover (a plain div of buttons) is positioned through the wrapper instead.
ARIA contract: the wrapper claims nothing — no `aria-haspopup` (it is not a button) and no role; `role="menu"` and
`role="menuitem"` (+ `tabindex="-1"`, hover `data-active`, ArrowUp/Down, typeahead) come from Flux's menu at runtime. Opened by
pointer, focus goes to the menu container (Escape and arrows work, nothing is pre-highlighted); opened by keyboard, focus goes to
the first enabled `[role=menuitem|menuitemcheckbox|menuitemradio]`. Screen-reader users do not discover right-click menus: keep the
same actions reachable elsewhere (a `<flux:dropdown>` button, row actions) — the context menu is a shortcut, never the only path.
Livewire contract: none of its own — no `wire:model`. Items take `wire:click` like any Flux menu item; the panel is teleported to
body, so a Livewire morph of the wrapped content never touches it.
```blade
<mds:context>
    <flux:card class="w-64">Right-click this card</flux:card>
    <mds:context.menu>
        <flux:menu>
            <flux:menu.item icon="pencil-square" wire:click="edit({{ $id }})">ویرایش</flux:menu.item>
            <flux:menu.item icon="document-duplicate" wire:click="duplicate({{ $id }})">تکثیر</flux:menu.item>
            <flux:menu.separator />
            <flux:menu.item icon="trash" variant="danger" wire:click="delete({{ $id }})">حذف</flux:menu.item>
        </flux:menu>
    </mds:context.menu>
</mds:context>
```

### <mds:pillbox> — multi-select with removable pills (open version of Flux Pro's flux:pillbox)
A combobox that keeps its chosen values as pills inside the control and filters a listbox of options as you type.
Props: `value` array|string|null (initial selection; an array, or a comma-separated string for plain forms) ·
`name` string|null (posts as `name[]`; also the key `$errors` is read with — defaults to the `wire:model` value) ·
`label` / `description` (flux:field chrome; `label` also names the listbox) · `placeholder` string|null (shown while
nothing is chosen) · `search-label` string|null (accessible name of the text field; defaults to `label`, else
'جستجو'/'Search' by fa) · `clearable` bool=false (a clear-all button, hidden while the selection is empty) ·
`max` int|null (selection cap; while it is reached every unchosen option goes `aria-disabled`) · `empty`
string|bool=true (no-match line: `true` = 'موردی یافت نشد.'/'No matches.' by fa, a string replaces it, `false`
hides the popup instead) · `disabled` bool=false · `invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (explicit message;
when omitted and `name` is set, falls back to `$errors->first($name)`) · `fa` bool|null=config (inherited by
options).
- `<mds:pillbox.option>` props: `value` string|null (defaults to the slot's text, so `PHP` selects "PHP") ·
  `disabled` bool=false · `fa`. Renders `role="option"` with `data-value` and a flattened `data-label`; markup
  inside the slot still renders, and a check icon marks a chosen row.
Behavior: typing filters with Persian normalization (Arabic ي/ك -> ی/ک; Persian/Arabic-Indic digits -> Latin before
matching); ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active option and wrap, Home/End jump, Enter or a click TOGGLES it and the
popup stays open (picking a second value is the point), Escape closes, Tab closes, Backspace on an empty query
takes the last pill off. Each pill has its own remove button ('حذف X'/'Remove X'); horizontal arrows are left to
the text caret on purpose. Disabled options stay visible but the cursor skips them. The option list is cached for
speed and follows the DOM: a MutationObserver on the listbox re-scans when a Livewire morph or an `x-for` adds,
removes or relabels options, keeping the cursor where it survives; `refresh()` on the Alpine component forces it.
ARIA contract: the text field is `role="combobox"` `aria-autocomplete="list"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`
-> the listbox and `aria-activedescendant` -> the active option (ids assigned at init). The popup holds
`role="listbox"` `aria-multiselectable="true"`; every option carries `aria-selected` plus a check icon, so
selection is never colour alone, and `aria-disabled` where it cannot be taken. A visually hidden `role="status"`
region announces the count («۲ مورد انتخاب شده» / "2 selected"); the no-match line is a second `role="status"`
OUTSIDE the listbox. The error message is `role="alert"` and is wired to the field with `aria-describedby`.
Livewire contract: the machine value is a visually hidden `<select multiple name="…[]">` whose selected options
mirror the pills — Livewire reads a multiple select as an array — and it is the element `wire:model*` is forwarded
to (the wrapper drops it). Every change rebuilds those options and dispatches a bubbling `input` AND `change`
event. A MutationObserver on that select re-reads it into Alpine state when the server rewrites the selection, so
`$this->tags = [...]` repaints the pills.
```blade
<mds:pillbox wire:model.live="tags" label="برچسب‌ها" placeholder="انتخاب کنید..." max="3" clearable>
    <mds:pillbox.option value="mobile">گوشی موبایل</mds:pillbox.option>
    <mds:pillbox.option value="books">کتاب و مجله</mds:pillbox.option>
    <mds:pillbox.option value="home" disabled>لوازم خانگی</mds:pillbox.option>
</mds:pillbox>
```

### <mds:editor> — rich-text field (open version of Flux Pro's flux:editor)
A `contenteditable` surface with a WAI-ARIA toolbar above it. No TipTap, no ProseMirror, no third-party
JavaScript at all: the marks are `document.execCommand` with a hand-written fallback for `formatBlock`,
and the value is sanitised down to a fixed allow-list on both sides of the surface.
Props: `name` string|null (plain form post + the key `$errors` is read with) · `value` string|null (stored HTML;
never echoed as markup — see below) · `placeholder` string|null · `label`/`description` (flux:field chrome;
`label` also names the surface) · `label:sr-only` / `description:sr-only` (Flux's colon syntax; `label-sr-only` /
`description-sr-only` are equivalent) · `toolbar` string|false|null=the default set (a space-separated tool list;
`|` is a separator; `false` renders no toolbar) · `toolbar-label` string|null (the toolbar's aria-label;
default 'نوار ابزار قالب‌بندی' / 'Formatting toolbar') · `rows` int=6 (starting height in lines, on the block axis) ·
`dir` ltr|rtl|auto|null (base direction of the surface; per-block direction is a toolbar tool) ·
`disabled` bool=false · `invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (explicit message; when omitted and `name` is
set, falls back to `$errors->first($name)`) · `fa` bool|null=config (inherited by toolbar/button/content).
Default slot replaces the built-in toolbar + content composition; the subcomponents share the parent's Alpine scope:
- `<mds:editor.toolbar>` props: `tools` string|array|null=the default set (`'bold italic underline strike | h1 h2 h3 | bullet ordered | quote code | link unlink | direction clear'`) · `label` (aria-label) · `fa`. Its own slot replaces the generated buttons.
- `<mds:editor.button>` props: `command` string|null (one of the tool names below, or null for a button you wire yourself) · `icon` string|null (defaults to the command's own icon) · `label` string|null (aria-label; defaults to the command's built-in name in the `fa` language) · `toggle` bool|null (defaults per command: true adds the reactive `aria-pressed`) · `fa`. Its slot replaces the icon.
- `<mds:editor.content>` props: `placeholder` · `rows` int=6 · `dir` · `label` (aria-label; default 'ویرایشگر متن' / 'Rich text editor') · `disabled` bool=false · `invalid` bool=false · `fa`. The `contenteditable` surface itself.
Tool names (aliases in brackets): `bold` · `italic` · `underline` · `strike` [strikethrough] · `h1` `h2` `h3` [heading1…] ·
`paragraph` [p] · `bullet` [ul, bullet-list] · `ordered` [ol, ordered-list, numbered] · `quote` [blockquote] ·
`code` [pre, code-block] (a `<pre>` block) · `link` · `unlink` · `direction` [dir, rtl] · `clear` [clear-format, remove-format].
Supported markup — the allow-list IS the feature set: `p h1 h2 h3 ul ol li blockquote pre strong em u s code a br`,
plus `href` on `a` (http/https/mailto/tel/ftp, fragments and relative paths only) and `dir="ltr|rtl"` on any block.
NOT supported: images, tables, colours, fonts, text alignment, inline styles, nested/indented lists, undo beyond the
browser's own, or collaborative editing. Anything else pasted is unwrapped to its text; `script`, `style`, `iframe`,
`img`, `form` controls and friends are dropped whole.
Behavior: `b`→`strong`, `i`→`em`, `div`→`p`, `h4-h6`→`h3` on the way in; a paste or a drop is filtered through the
same sanitiser before it is inserted (parsed in a detached `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument`, so nothing
loads or runs even in the markup being thrown away); empty blocks left behind by the browser are pruned, and a
deliberate blank line (`<p><br></p>`) survives. `link` asks for a URL with `window.prompt`, prefixes a bare host with
`https://`, refuses anything else with a scheme, and links the URL itself when nothing is selected. Block tools toggle:
pressing `h2` inside an `<h2>` returns the block to `<p>`. `direction` flips the current block's `dir` between ltr and
rtl. `clear` removes the inline marks and links, and returns a heading/quote/code block to a paragraph.
Shortcuts: Ctrl/⌘+B, +I, +U, +K (link), +\ (clear), +Shift+X (strikethrough), +Shift+7 (numbered list),
+Shift+8 (bulleted list). Tab is deliberately not captured — it leaves the surface.
ARIA contract: the toolbar is `role="toolbar"` with `aria-label` and `aria-controls` -> the surface, one tab stop with a
roving tabindex (Left/Right follow the VISUAL order — read from `getComputedStyle().direction` at keydown, so they stay
previous/next on an RTL page — plus Home/End and wrap-around). Toggle tools carry a reactive `aria-pressed` recomputed
from the selection on every `selectionchange`; `link`, `unlink` and `clear` act once and carry none. Separators are
`role="separator"` `aria-orientation="vertical"`. Buttons cancel `mousedown`, so clicking one never takes the selection.
The surface is `role="textbox"` `aria-multiline="true"`, named by `label`, `aria-invalid` when invalid, with a
`focus-visible` ring on the whole box. Disabled applies `inert` + `aria-disabled` and `contenteditable="false"`.
Livewire contract: `wire:model` is forwarded to a hidden input holding the sanitised HTML (everything else lands on the
root `[data-mds-editor]` div); every change writes it and dispatches a bubbling `input` event. The stored value is
NEVER rendered as markup — it reaches the page as an escaped attribute and Alpine paints it onto the surface through the
sanitiser, so a value poisoned elsewhere cannot execute. The surface carries `wire:ignore` (a morph would otherwise
diff the server's empty div against what has been typed), and a `MutationObserver` on the hidden input's `value`
attribute repaints the surface when the server changes the bound property; both are torn down in `destroy()`.
An empty editor commits `''`, not `<p><br></p>`.
Data attributes: `data-mds-editor` (root) · `-toolbar` · `-tool` + `-command="bold"` · `-separator` · `-body` ·
`-content` (the surface) · `-placeholder` · `-input` (the hidden control).
```blade
<form wire:submit="save">
    <mds:editor wire:model="body" name="body" label="متن آگهی" description="حداکثر ۵۰۰ کلمه"
                placeholder="داستان محصول را بنویسید..." rows="8" dir="rtl"
                toolbar="bold italic | h2 h3 | bullet ordered | link unlink | direction clear" />
    <flux:button type="submit" variant="primary" class="mt-3">ذخیره</flux:button>
</form>
```
The value is HTML you still have to trust on the server: the sanitiser runs in the browser, so validate and re-sanitise
before storing or echoing it (`{!! !!}` on unvalidated user HTML is a stored-XSS hole whatever the editor did).

### <mds:calendar> — date picker grid, Jalali by default (open version of Flux Pro's flux:calendar)
The point of the component: Flux's calendar is Gregorian, this one is Jalali (`MajidDs\Support\Jalali`), with the Gregorian grid
still one prop away. Machine values are ALWAYS ISO Gregorian `Y-m-d` with Latin digits, whatever the grid draws.
Props: `value` string|DateTimeInterface|array|null (mode `range` takes `[start, end]` or `['start' => …, 'end' => …]`; mode
`multiple` takes an array; anything `MajidDs\Support\Persian::toDateTime()` parses) · `mode` single|multiple|range='single'
(an unknown value falls back to `single`) · `min` / `max` date|null (out-of-bounds days get `aria-disabled` and also disable the
month arrows) · `unavailable` array=[] (individual dates disabled inside the bounds) · `months` int=1 (clamped to 1…12; grids
wrap in a flex row, each with its own `<caption>`) · `calendar` jalali|gregorian='jalali' · `start-day` int|null=null
(0=Sunday … 6=Saturday; defaults to 6 for Jalali, 1 for Gregorian) · `week-numbers` bool=false (a `<th scope="row">` column
counting from the week that holds the 1st of the calendar's OWN year) · `fixed-weeks` bool=false (always six rows, so the box
never changes height between months) · `selectable-header` bool=false (month + year `<select>`s instead of the title) ·
`with-today` bool=false (a "today" shortcut under the grid; in `single` mode it also selects today) · `static` bool=false
(read-only: `aria-readonly`, no picking, no range hover preview) · `size` sm|lg|null=null (cell 7/8/10) · `name` string|null
(plain form post: `name` for single, `name[]` for multiple, `name[start]`/`name[end]` for range — and the key the error bag is
read with) · `label` string|null='تقویم'/'Calendar' by fa (the grid's accessible name; multi-month grids get «label — month») ·
`invalid` bool=false · `error` string|null (see Validation contract — renders the message) · `fa` bool|null=config.
`fa` and `calendar` are independent axes: a Jalali grid in English (Farvardin, Latin digits) and a Gregorian grid in Persian
(ژانویه, Persian digits) are both valid, exactly as `mds:jalali-date` behaves.
Behavior: the server renders a complete grid — selection, today, disabled days, roving tabindex — so the page is correct before
Alpine boots and without it; Alpine then redraws the same shape from `window.mds.jalali` (`mds::partials.jalali`, the JS port of
`MajidDs\Support\Jalali`) and hides the server copy. Month arrows step one month; clicking a greyed neighbouring day brings that
month on screen so a selection is never off-grid. Range mode: first click opens the span, second closes it, either order (a
backwards pair is straightened out), and the pointer previews the span before the second click. Multiple mode toggles days and
keeps them sorted. All date arithmetic runs on integer day serials, never `Date`, so DST cannot skip or repeat a day.
ARIA contract: each month is a `<table role="grid">` named by `label`, `aria-readonly` when `static`, `aria-describedby` the error
when there is one; rows are `role="row"`, cells `role="gridcell"` carrying `aria-selected`, weekday headers `<th scope="col">`
with the initial `aria-hidden` beside the full name in an `.sr-only` span, week numbers `<th scope="row">`. Each day is a
`<button>` with the full spoken date as `aria-label` («پنجشنبه ۲۹ مرداد ۱۴۰۵»), `aria-current="date"` on today, `aria-disabled`
(never the `disabled` attribute — disabled days stay reachable) and `data-date` with the ISO value. Roving tabindex: exactly one
cell is tabbable — the selection when it is on screen, else today, else the 1st of the first month. Keyboard on the grid:
Arrow keys ±1 day / ±1 week (Left/Right follow the VISUAL order — `direction` is read at keydown, so an RTL island in an LTR page
still moves the way the arrow points), Home/End jump to the start/end of the week, PageUp/PageDown ±1 month, Shift+PageUp/PageDown
±1 year. The header title is an `aria-live="polite"` region so a month change is announced.
Livewire contract: `wire:model*` never lands on the wrapper; it reaches the hidden control, once, per mode —
`single` → `<input type="hidden" x-ref="input">`; `multiple` → a visually-hidden `<select multiple name="x[]">` whose options
mirror the selection (Livewire reads a multiple select as an array); `range` → two hidden inputs bound to dotted paths under the
caller's property, modifiers kept (`wire:model.live="trip"` → `trip.start` / `trip.end`). Every commit dispatches bubbling
`input` and `change` events. A `MutationObserver` on the hidden control re-reads a server-changed value back into Alpine after a
morph, and is disconnected in `destroy()`.
Styling hooks: `data-mds-calendar` on the root (plus `data-mds-calendar-mode` / `-system`, and `data-invalid` / `data-static`),
`-header` `-prev` `-next` `-title` `-selects` `-month-select` `-year-select` `-months` `-month` `-week` `-day` `-today`
`-start` `-end` `-select`; each day carries `data-selected` `data-in-range` `data-range-start` `data-range-end` `data-today`
`data-outside` `data-disabled` as they apply.
Example:
```blade
<mds:calendar wire:model.live="deliverAt" name="deliver_at" :min="now()" :max="now()->addDays(30)"
    :unavailable="['2026-08-28']" with-today week-numbers label="روز تحویل" />

<mds:calendar mode="range" wire:model="trip" :months="2" fixed-weeks />   {{-- trip.start / trip.end --}}
<mds:calendar mode="multiple" wire:model="days" selectable-header />      {{-- an array of ISO dates --}}
<mds:calendar calendar="gregorian" :start-day="0" static :value="$order->shipped_at" />
```

## CSS layer (resources/css/mds.css)

- No `@theme` and no font: the kit does not set `--font-sans` or load a face. See Fonts.
- `[x-cloak] { display: none !important }` — the ONE rule kept outside `@layer components` on purpose: it must beat whatever the
  component sets while Alpine boots. Everything below is inside `@layer components`, so any Tailwind utility a caller adds wins
  (a test walks the stylesheet's top level and fails on any other unlayered rule).
- `[dir='rtl'] input[type='tel'], [dir='rtl'] input[data-ltr]` — direction:ltr, text-align:end (phone/code inputs).
- `.mds-checker` — checkerboard backdrop for transparent colors; tokens `--mds-checker-dark` / `--mds-checker-light`, with a `.dark` pairing.
- `.mds-range` — gradient range-slider styling (color-picker hue/alpha); thumb via `--mds-thumb` (dark pairing), and its own
  `:focus-visible` ring because `appearance: none` drops the native one.
- `[data-mds-icon] ...` — icon default size (1.5rem) and the opt-in `--mds-icon-stroke` rule.
- `[data-mds-timeline] ...` — the timeline grid, connector lines and indicator states. Cascade layers outrank specificity, so if this
  were unlayered it would swallow classes users put on an indicator (e.g. `bg-green-500`).
- `[data-mds-chart] ...` — chart card chrome, stages, tracks and the heatmap tone ladder.
  The chart ink is currentColor: the stage sets zinc-950/white and every fill/stroke is an opacity step of it,
  so a text utility (`text-accent`) on a stage recolors the whole chart. Knobs: `--mds-chart-radius` (card,
  1.5rem), `--mds-chart-stage` (stage background, also the halo behind line dots).

## Shared script (resources/views/partials/digits.blade.php)

`@include('mds::partials.digits')` registers `window.mds.digits(value, fa = true)` (Latin -> Persian digits, display-only) and
`window.mds.latinDigits(value)` (Persian/Arabic-Indic -> Latin, for reading typed input back). It is wrapped in `@once('mds-digits')`,
so however many components pull it in, it is emitted once per page. Included by quantity, countdown, composer, file-upload and
command; it is the JS twin of `Persian::digits()` / `latinDigits()`. Served from the package's `mds::` view namespace — it is not
part of the `mds-views` publish tag and needs no publishing.

## Page layouts (Flux grid; demo: workbench /layouts)

The element that directly wraps `<flux:main>` becomes a 3x3 grid (rule lives in flux.css):

    grid-template-areas: "header  header  header"
                         "sidebar main    aside"
                         "sidebar footer  aside";

If `<flux:sidebar>` precedes `<flux:header>`, the first row becomes `"sidebar header header"` — sidebar full
height, header beside it. Put `<flux:header>` first instead and the header spans the full width. Nothing else
changes; child order picks the arrangement. In RTL the sidebar lands on the right automatically.

- `<flux:header sticky container>` — sticky pins it and caps its height; container centres content at max-w-7xl.
- `<flux:sidebar sticky collapsible>` — collapses to an icon rail on desktop; pair with `<flux:sidebar.collapse />`.
- `<flux:sidebar sticky collapsible="mobile">` — fixed on desktop, off-canvas below `lg`; open it with
  `<flux:sidebar.toggle class="lg:hidden" icon="bars-2" />` (backdrop is rendered by flux:sidebar itself).
- `<flux:aside sticky class="w-80">` — third column, spans the main+footer rows; give it a width yourself.
- `<flux:main container>`, `<flux:footer container>`, `<flux:container>` — width control; `<flux:spacer />` pushes
  header actions to the far end.
- Sidebar body: `sidebar.header`, `sidebar.brand`, `sidebar.search`, `sidebar.nav`, `sidebar.item`, `sidebar.group`
  (`expandable`, `expanded`), `sidebar.spacer`, `sidebar.profile`. Top nav: `navbar` + `navbar.item`, with
  `navmenu` inside a `dropdown` for mobile.
- Persian labels: pass `tooltip="..."` to `sidebar.collapse` and `aria-label="..."` to `sidebar.toggle`; their
  defaults are English.

## Rules of thumb for generated code

- Prefer `<mds:*>` and `<flux:*>` components over raw HTML in Blade views.
- Use logical utilities (ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/start-/end-) — never ml-/mr-/left-/right- — so RTL keeps working.
- Money: never hardcode number_format for prices; use <mds:price>, @toman/@rial, or Persian::money().
- Dates shown to users: Jalali via <mds:jalali-date> or Mds::jalali(); machine values stay Gregorian ISO.
- Keep phone/OTP/code inputs LTR: type="tel" or data-ltr attribute.
- Persian digits are display-only; anything submitted/bound stays Latin (the components already guarantee this).
- Flux free components available alongside (32): avatar, badge, brand, breadcrumbs, button, callout, card, checkbox,
  dropdown/menu, field, heading, icon, input, modal, navbar, navlist, navmenu, otp-input, pagination, profile, progress,
  radio, select, separator, skeleton, switch, table, text, textarea, toast, toggle, tooltip. Flux Pro-only components NOT available
  unless licensed: autocomplete, calendar, date-picker, editor, tabs, etc. — use mds:command,
  mds:color-picker, mds:file-upload, mds:timeline and mds:chart instead of flux:command / flux:color-picker /
  flux:file-upload / flux:timeline / flux:chart (different API: mds:chart is server-rendered SVG, not a
  wire:model-driven client chart).
- File sizes shown to users: <mds:file-item :size="$bytes" /> or Persian::fileSize() — never a hand-rolled KB/MB formatter.
- Icons: prefer <mds:icon icon="..." /> with a Hugeicons name (hugeicons.com) over raw <svg> or <flux:icon>.
  Heroicon names still resolve, so existing markup needs no rewrite.
